[h1]"Gameplay and story are still the same standard. Unmemorable characters with no development, anticlimatic story, same graphics and very similar gameplay."[/h1]

First off I'll say I am a loyal Assassins Creed fan and a dedicated PC gamer. I have also completed every Assassin's Creed game to date on PC. This is my personal opinion, being very picky, and coming from the perspective of a long time Assassins Creed fan;

[u] PORT WISE [/u]
I can say that it runs MUCH better than AC Unity does. I have a GTX 780 ti and everything is always perfectly smooth with all settings maxed out (at least 50-60 fps). I would get ridiculous random stutters on AC Unity. (Unfortunately, because these are console ports you won't be getting much more than that.)

For the first time in an AC game I feel Ubisoft has actually put forth effort with regard to the PC port (Unlike every other developer, I'm looking at you, Bethesda). Unfortunately these days the gaming industry is more aimed at consoles. However they have actually removed mouse lag/mouse acceleration so navigating menus, moving camera around etc is more responsive. AC Unity was a headache to navigate around. Not surprising as they received ALOT of backfire from AC Unity last year.

The user interface could be toned down a bit. It has definitely been improved since AC Unity however there are some things that are just not needed/should be implemented in a different way. For example the detection ring around the character, enemy levels above their head etc.


[u] GAMEPLAY WISE [/u]
Pretty much the same as any other Assassin's Creed game. Small improvements are made with regard to navigation, combat and stealth. The rope launcher feels like its needed as the streets are wider. Combat feels more responsive and fast paced. However it still feels like a constant 'click fest'. Stealth is made more simple with a simpler cover system. HOWEVER I believe the enemy detection system requires an overhaul. Silently kidnap an enemy, and suddenly 10 enemy carriages appear from nowhere and chase you down. Same with killing an enemy via a ranged weapon. Every enemy in the area is suddenly aware of your presence.
With regard to side content, I honestly believe they should stop adding in 'stuff to do for the sake of stuff to do'. There are alot of icons on the map and most if not all of these activites require you to 'kill/kidnap this enemy'. I wish they'd bring back old school Assassination contracts.

[u] STORY WISE **SPOILERS** [/u]
It seems to be the same protocol every year for Assassins Creed in regard to the story; create a likeable, humorous protagonist that defeats the bad guy (Since ACIV at least). 
I can say that I believe Jacob and Evie were not introduced very well. Start up a new game and you're all of a sudden assassinating enemies as Jacob. We don't know where he's from, what his motives are or what situation he's in. Its hard to describe.
I feel I do not always agree with the motives and feelings of the protagonists. Yes, they are freeing slaves, liberating London etc but I think it takes more than that to make you want to progress further.

You need to feel the emotions the protagonist is feeling. These characters have no motivation at all other than simply 'going after the bad guy because he is bad', which is lazy character development. Ezio, Edward and even Connor were perfect examples. They weren't simply 'going after the bad guy', they had realistic goals/motives. As much as Jacob and Evie are 'likeable' characters, there is simply no character development, the protagonists do not 'learn anything new' from their adventures, and their stories are rather abruptly ended. But YES they are somewhat likeable.

At the start of the game we are introduced to the big bad guy, Crawford Starrick, that is trying to control London and 'must be killed'. So without hesitation Jacob and Evie go after him and eventually kill him. They are thanked by the queen and the game ends. WTF? No epic plot twist or cliffhangers? Come on Ubisoft, this is the most boring, unexciting and predictable story yet. As much as I hate to say it, but even AC Unity had a more exciting story.
There are characters that COULD have been interesting/memorable like Henry Green, but unfortunately only have a few lines of dialogue.

Once again I believe the modern day story is lacking. You can tell that Ubisoft is simply trying to appeal to a wider audience by almost ditching the modern day story. On a positive note, I am glad they decided to include Juno in the storyline this time. But they really need to step up their game in regard to the modern day story. Give us a character to control, don't throw these 5 minute cutscenes at us.

[u] BOTTOM LINE [/u]
I do not feel like an Assassin anymore. Instead I feel more like a gang leader or a street thug in a 'beat em up' game, which I think is wrong. In my opinion, Ubisoft needs to stop and think to themselves 'Okay, what does being an assassin actually mean?'. Assassins are supposed to hide from the general public. Instead we are openly starting gang wars. Assassins are supposed to be feared. Every enemy treats you like they are not scared at all. Taunting/intimidating you as you walk by. Remember that time in AC2 when you killed Uberto Alberti in open public? Everyone was shocked. Civilians were terrified. Assassinations need to be like that.
Assassins are also supposed to be a 'brotherhood'. Where were all the other assassins in London?

This is a great Assassins Creed game and I recommend it. Unfortunately, because its one of Ubisoft's best selling franchises, they feel the need to release annually which results in similar recycled content each year. Ubisoft really needs to go back to the 'core' of the franchise and make an effort to appeal to long time fans, NOT just always 'casual gamers' every year.

I don't understand why so many people think AC Syndicate "made up for what AC Unity did wrong". On the technical side, yes, it runs much smoother. But gameplay and story are still the same standard. Unmemorable characters with no development, anticlimatic story, same graphics, very similar gameplay.

So YES, I recommend Assassin's Creed Syndicate. But don't expect huge improvements or anything revolutionary.

At the time of writing this review, I only have a few hours on this game on PC.  But rest assured, I had hit almost 100% on console prior to purchasing this on Steam.

This installment in the series was a HUGE step in the right direction, in terms of both story and gameplay.  I have a slight obsession with the AC series, and everything since AC3 just didn't really "feel" like AC.  This game, to me, began a turnaround back to the great character stories and dialogue we've come to expect and love from the AC series.  The game doesn't take any time at all slogging through a detailed character background sequence as per usual; it gets right into the meat of the game and lets you learn the character stories along the way.

This game is also optimized much better than Black Flag or Unity, and Victorian London with graphics at full blast in 4k is absolutely stunning.

One of the more common complaints I've seen is that the combat is too arcade-y and the addition of the grappling hook makes the game "too unrealistic".  I'd like to address these...

1. The combat is much faster.  Beyond that, I don't really see how it's more arcade-like unless you consider all the others arcade-like as well.  Be honest with yourself, how many times have you found yourself in an AC game finishing a fight and suddenly finding Altair/Ezio/Connor/Edward/Arno standing in an overly large pile of corpses?

2. As far as the grappling hook making the game "unrealistic", I would like to remind those critics that a core element of every AC game has involved jumping dozens to hundreds of feet/meters off of buildings INTO PILES OF HAY.

I digress.  If you are a fan of AC, and you weren't really into AC3 or Unity, and you shared my concerns about the direction of the series, I recommend this game.  And I recommend that you play it all the way through, including the side story stuff.

[h1]Twin Assassins[/h1]

Released just a year after its predecessor Syndicate - for the first time in the series - sports two protagonists. We can switch between Jacob and Evie as we see fit; during cutscenes they'll both be present, though. However, memory sequences include missions, too, for each of them, separately. We get to know both of them very well not to mention their struggle with the creed and with each other.

[h1]Victoria Era London[/h1]

Unity was ambitious. Constantly seeing the mob in front of the Palais de Justice was great. Making friends with Bonaparte. Who could refuse such a thing? Syndicate shows us a different world - London slowly being taken over by Templar Crawford Starrick who controls businesses as well as organised crime. The Fryes - against Brotherhood orders - go to the capital to teach Starrick a lesson. You will appreciate the new, "moving" headquarters, your very own train. No real estates this time.

[h1]Rooks, Carriages And That Rope Launcher[/h1]

You will regularly bump into street gangs, the so-called Blighters. London consists of 7 huge areas that are, initially, completely red. Secondary missions such as killing Templars, liberating children from factories or kidnapping key criminals and by doing so aiding the Scotland Yard will all be tasks available to reduce the Templar presence. Completing all side missions will open up the final war mission where you will have the opportunity to face the gang boss.

And this is where Syndicate shines: the opportunity to make secondary quests vital to the main story. As you clear up the streets there will be more and more criminals dressed in green instead of red. They are the Rooks and they are yours to command. Your regular income can be used to make them stronger, appear in greater numbers and you can even become so notorious that bad guys dare not attack you any more.

Horse-pulled carriages are a common sight in Syndicate and the related cargo escort and -hijack missions will be randomly (but constantly) generated. This introduces vehicular combat and an easier (and faster way) to navigate the streets of London. Making friends with Graham Bell will get you the rope launcher - consider it the AC version of Batman's grappling hook. You don't swing, though: you need to press the button so that your character can slide and find themselves on the rooftop of the opposite building in a matter of seconds. 

[h1]The Thames, Skills And Collectibles[/h1]

Remember those games where you needed to cross the road with an animal? Imagine this now on the River Thames. Boats are constantly moving and appearing in front of you. Its fun hopping over to the other side and while doing so sabotaging the cargo of some Templar gang or simply marking loot for your fellow gang members. 

As in Unity we have to keep playing to earn XP and obtain skill points. Purchasing various skills and their better (upgraded) versions will allow us to attain a higher level. Achievement hunters and those who like exploring everything will be disappointed to see level 10 is the maximum we can reach. Halfway through the game we already have everything. I also missed the minigame concerning lock picking. There are some skills that are only available for Jacob or for Evie. The latter was the one I preferred as Jacob is a tad bit "brute" and Evie's extra skills are more akin to that of an assassin.

As for collectibles we now look for flowers, taste various types of beers, collect royal correspondence and the ever-present Helix glitches and treasure chests will also return. For most maps are available for purchase if you are tired of looking. We also have craft materials: extra resources are available as some inventory items cannot be immediately found but only crafted. This usually requires that we obtain the related schematics. 

As for weapons: a great assortment of kukris, brass knuckles and cape-swords are available. Fighting involves a lot of finishing animations - watching a film to see how Evie takes down 4 approaching enemies one after the other is just beautiful. Boxing events are available for practising. Certain activities during combat have built-in counters - performing, for instance, 25 double assassinations will make you stronger. There are a lot of such perks available - you really need to complete all missions, explore everything and play as varied a way as possible to become the ultimate assassin. 

[h1]AnvilNext 2.0 And Multiplayer[/h1]

The new AnvilNext engine debuted in Unity and it was not properly optimised as it had a lot of bugs and glitches. All is well now and Syndicate's 19th century London looks tremendously beautiful. Certain missions take place at night and facial expressions of each character (including NPCs) are getting better and better. Female antagonists in the ranks of the Blighters and children on the streets of London will be a common sight. Kids will get you items as you help them - Syndicate gives you associates who regularly give you missions. It's best to complete all for getting extra weapons, cloaks, belts or weapon schematics.

Multiplayer - for the first time in many years - is completely non-existent. No coop or companion app, either. Following the issues of Unity we were promised a better story. And Syndicate has a better one, actually. Both Fryes are likeable and, as usual, we meet many celebrities. Graham Bell gives us bombs, Sergeant Abberline always goes undercover to meet us, we realise Churchill did some great things even during World War I and we also meet Karl Marx, Charles Dickens, Darwin and even get knighted by the Queen herself.

[h1]Nothing Is True...[/h1]

It may be so but with Syndicate I've had most fun since Black Flag. I cannot comment on the DLCs, unfortunately, but I had fun while slowly taking over London, climbing up the Big Ben and chasing crazy suicidal Templars in the Houses of Parliament.  I achieved 100% synchronisation in 75 hours and I did not regret any second of it. The gameplay mechanics are getting better and better and I look forward to seeing the nextgen AC games by downloading Origins.

Victorian Era London is a beautiful setting for an Assassin's Creed game. I believe Syndicate is an underrated installment in the series. Both Evie and Jacob Frye are fun to play as and the missions are quite enjoyable. This is the last "OG" Assassin's Creed game before Ubisoft took it into the RPG genre with Origins, so it actually feels like an Assassin's Creed game. 10/10 highly recommend!. I know the world may have forgotten you AC: Syndicate, but I love you.

Biggest AC fan from the beginning, played the first games like crazy. Quality started to decline dramatically with Revelations and hit a low with Unity. That brings us to Syndicate.

I had huge hopes for Syndicate. It seemed like they were trying to improve a lot of things. The gameplay did actually improve quite a bit. It's like the Assassin's Creediest Assassin's Creed in that matter. 

However, the story is hard to follow, because you don't get emotionally attached to the main characters a lot. They're trying to pull of the same things over and over again, but they just aren't pulling through. The problem with the series is that they try to get so much detail by adding open houses, a lot of foliage and decoration and a lot of historical facts. They fail to add detail to the characters and especially the people surrounding you, though.

Take Black Flag as an example. The Jackdaws crew was just there. You neither had to find a steerer, a cannoneer, a carpenter nor the bloody Spanish cook, that was mentioned in the book. Image you would've had to actually put together a crew and take actual care of your men or women. The same goes for the rooks in Syndicate. You have a couple of important persons on your team, but they're too distant like the other captains in Black Flag and it's not like you'd actually care about that fat lady in the chair.

Also, you don't get attached to the main characters. In Assassin's Creed III you had at least a little attachment to Connor. You saw his parents, you saw him growing up, you experienced his childhood horrors and his relentless way of becoming an Assassin. Sure, you cannot top Ezio in Assassin's Creed II. You experienced the whole process of him growing up from a cocky teenager who didn't know anything about the world to a caring and calm adult. Whilst you knew every single one of your allies by doing stuff with or for them. The recent AC titles lack this sort of dedication to the main characters. 

Then there's just too much content. Ubisoft emphasises the amount of playable content in the latest AC games, starting with Black Flag. According to Ubi, you were able to spent 80 hours in Black Flag until completion. Well, but do you want to? At least 40% of the completion rate is just farming chests and other collectibles. This part became even bigger in Unity, where you could find almost ten different items throughout every single district. In my opinion that is no content at all. It doesn't affect me, my playstyle, the story line or the character development. If you're on the first playthrough and try to get full sync in the missions, you can make it through Black Flag in 16 hours and that is fine. But advertising and fooling players into buying the game through a cheap trick like posing collectibles for content won't make for a great game. 

And finally the technical part of Syndicate. Making a game that's full of details and that has sophisticated graphics is one thing. Making a game that can be run on a normal PC or console with a smooth experience is another. Not being able to play a game on full settings has been used for ads once, especially with Crysis. But that time is long gone. I've been trying to run Syndicate on a 4x3,5ghz processor, 16gb HyperX Fury and a GTX980 and I'm actually getting bluescreens. Bluescreens? That was the first bluescreen I've ever seen on the new Windows! Even on medium graphics it's just slow, buggy and glitchy. Especially horse carriage missions are horrible. Just like in Watch Dogs, the game cannot load the next parts of the map fast enough. 

Well, Mr Smartass, can you even make a game that meets your tremendous demands? Yes, you can. Take the Mass Effect series for example. Mass Effect 3 looked pretty good at that time and it ran smoothly even on a fucking laptop. I've played the demo at the CeBit a couple of months before the launch of ME3. All they offered us were ASUS gaming laptops, but you were able to push settings to max and get your full 60fps without the computer even getting loud. And you were attached to all those charakters throughout the entirety of the series. You will remember Admiral Anderson, Liara and Garrus for the rest of your life, wont you? But you'll have forgotten about Jacob and Evie long before you play your last games. 

You don't need the best graphics, the best story or the best gameplay to make a great game. All it takes is a good idea and the best you can do out of it. The latest games of this series however, Assassin's Creed Syndicate included, just lack passion and heart. And if you know a little about the development of these games, then you know why.

Syndicate is great. Not perfect, not a best game since ac2, but pretty great. City is vast, detailed and beautiful. Main characters are charming and make a good duo. Gameplay, as always, somewhat the same, somewhat new and interesting(first time I saw rope launcher I thought "Oh, they're making it easier, that'll kill parkour, this series is done for!", but 5 minutes later I found myself joyfully zipping and zapping on that thing all over the place). Quality of the story is subjective, but I enjoyed it. A step back from epic battles and world-shaking revolutions felt nice. Modern time storyline is still told through CG cinematics, but actually kinda matters this time. The game looks gorgeous too, just as good as unity, but optimized a bit better this time, haven't encountered any terrible fps drops or a single bug. 

You could've skipped Unity, but you should buy Syndicate. It's well worth it.

VERDICT:
Being a British fellow myself, I found this game very relatable when it came to London itself. Most things were in the right place, with the atmosphere being how I would picture it back in the 1800 (Aside from Assassin's running around). The story didn't live up to some of the other Assassin's Creeds but the gameplay was very smooth and adding my new favourite gimmick (The Zipline) gave it a more fresh approach. 

What I enjoyed the most out of this game would be the voice acting and how the characters reacted to certain things, just walking across the street was entertaining! This is the closest they get to the modern era and i'm very relieved that they stopped it here... in London.

GAMEPLAY:
It is the ninth major instalment in the Assassin's Creed series, and the successor to 2014's Assassin's Creed Unity.

The plot follows the premise of the Assassin's Creed franchise, involving a fictional history of real-world events where a secret war has been fought for centuries between two factions: the Brotherhood of Assassins, who promote peace and liberty, and the Templar Order, who desire peace through control. The framing story is set in the 21st century and follows the same unnamed and unseen protagonist from Assassin's Creed Unity, who assists the Assassins in their race against the Templars to find an artefact hidden in London. The main story is set in London in 1868, at the onset of the Second Industrial Revolution, and follows twin Assassins Jacob and Evie Frye as they navigate the corridors of organised crime and take back the city from Templar control.

The game is played from a third-person perspective and its open world is navigated on foot or by carriage. The game introduces new travelling systems and refined combat and stealth mechanics. Players control the two lead protagonists throughout the game's story, switching between them both during and outside of missions

Phenomenal entry for the franchise : removed a lot of frustrating aspects of the gameplay while keeping the fun in.

I'll just list some examples to illustrate the point.
Tired of spending the first ten hours in-game for the the same 'Discovering the Brotherhood' plot?
The Frye twins are raised Assassins - you start the game with the hidden blades

Tired of spending cumulative hours of your life climbing towers?
You've a Rope Dart launcher that helps you climb and set up ziplines.

Can't reliably set up air assassinations and you're sick of waiting for the wonky guard patrol path?
The same ziplines practically helps you set up air assassinations anywhere.

Forced to travel to different regions / soft-locked out of parts of the map for lore reasons?
You're free to complete the activities before doing any main sequence missions 

Fantastic setting as well with no shortage of things to do.
Bored of running or even using fast travel? Board the train and go sightseeing mode before hopping off your train at the station.
Absolutely HATE swimming in Assassin's Creed games? Hop on a merchant ship along the Thames or raid rival ships for cargo to pass the time.

All that said it's still an Assassin's Creed game so there might be visual bugs or dummy NPC interactions once in a while.
If you're willing to tolerate the occasional off-sync fight animations and NPCs being stupid, this is honestly a great game.

[code]Assassin’s Creed: Syndicate is a farewell to the classic Assassin’s Creed formula, with all the ups and downs one might expect from that by now[/code]

At its launch in 2015, [i]Assassin’s Creed Syndicate[/i] might’ve been met with a more critical reception amongst some players than it might receive today. The reason is simple: At this point in time, there had been at least one [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] release every year (since 2009) and – not surprisingly, considering the short development time – each of these iterations differed very little from another. Players understandably grew tired of playing through the same game every year and especially after the [url= https://steamcommunity.com/id/dreamylotus/recommended/289650/]rough launch of Unity[/url] one year prior, the general anticipation for a new [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] title – which would be [i]Syndicate[/i] – was not particularly high.

As a result, publisher Ubisoft decided that the franchise was in need of some major reinvention, which in turn led to a two-year break before the next main title released in 2017: [i]Assassin’s Creed Origins[/i]. And indeed, [i]Origins[/i] was a completely overhauled [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] game in many regards, including a different gameplay loop, which now featured many RPG elements. This makes [i]Syndicate[/i] the last main game in the franchise to feature the “classic” [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] gameplay (until the upcoming release of [i]Assassin’s Creed Mirage[/i] in October 2023, that is).

This could mean that [i]Syndicate[/i] – being the last of its kind – is the classic [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] formula honed to its perfection, both in terms of gameplay and story. But while [i]Syndicate[/i] might be an improvement upon its predecessor [i]Unity[/i], it’s really not much different (or even better) than what came before. In fact, almost all of the usual criticism applies to [i]Syndicate[/i] as well.

What could’ve been a gamechanger is the new protagonist duo, the assassin twins Evie and Jacob Frye. Evie’s strength lies in being stealthy, while Jacob is more focused on combat. They both got separate equipment and skill trees, which sounds bigger than it really is: The skill trees are the same save for a few unique ones, experience points are shared, and you’ll share most of the equipment as well (e.g. guns). But what’s most disappointing is that this supposed duo only acts as a duo during exactly one (!) story mission, where you’ll switch between both characters. All other story missions are focused on one of twins and the game forces you to play as said twin during these missions.

This would’ve been disappointing but fine if the twins had equal screentime at least. But looking at the base game, this [url=https://gamerant.com/assassins-creed-syndicate-evie-jacob-screentime/]isn’t the case either[/url]: You’ll play as Jacob for roughly two-thirds of the main missions, while Evie is only left with the remaining third. [i]Syndicate[/i] clearly has a favorite twin and it isn’t shy about that.

Story-wise, the whole twin dynamic is quite messy as well, with forced character arcs and a lot of “but father said…”. There aren’t a lot of games with twins both being playable protagonists, so it’s a shame that [i]Syndicate[/i] doesn’t really make use of this opportunity at all, in both gameplay and story. Though considering the story is riddled with its own problems, that’s hardly surprising.

[i]Syndicate[/i] does not only suffer from the usual story problems of open-world games (mainly pacing issues and unnecessary roadblocks like “do X side activities in order to continue the main story”) but also fails as an [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] story. The brotherhood is mentioned at the beginning as Jacob & Evie take things into their own hands, going against their orders, but that whole plot point never comes up again. Including the twins, there are only three assassins present in the entirety of London, [i]Syndicate[/i]’s setting, when even the Caribbean Sea was filled with assassins in [i]Black Flag[/i]. There’s a lot of templars to take down, sure, but they’re forgettable villains with the only templar connection of being called one.

As for the modern-day story, the Phoenix Project story of the [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] games since [i]Black Flag[/i] continues – through small cutscenes between story chapters. But considering the entire Phoenix Project story was only continued (& finished) through a [url=https://assassinscreed.fandom.com/wiki/Assassin%27s_Creed:_Uprising]comic book series[/url] after the release of [i]Syndicate[/i], it should already be clear that Ubisoft didn’t really care about it in the end.

Overall, the main story of [i]Syndicate[/i] works in terms of telling you where to go next and why but it’s not much more than that. I feel like it could’ve been so much more if the twins were properly used and the villains (as well as the assassins) more fleshed out but in the end, it’s the usual quest to take down a bad guy’s minions in order to finally tackle the bag guy himself. While I’m on the topic: [i]Syndicate[/i] also got one of the most boring final battles I ever encountered in a videogame. I couldn’t help but think “wait, that’s it??” as the final cutscenes started rolling.

In terms of gameplay, [i]Syndicate[/i] is basically [i]Unity[/i] with some improvements. Instead of being stuck running around the city, [i]Syndicate[/i] offers horse carriages and a grappling hook to get through the city of London. Both are well appreciated since the city’s big and the fast travel points are few. The grappling hook is more of a hit-or-miss, however, since you can’t really properly control its target.

The rest of the game is really the usual mix of chasing people, tailing people, killing people and interacting with certain objects. There’s a lot of side content one could indulge in but considering it’s all just the same few objectives repeated over and over again, I don’t really see any reason to do so. That said, combat and parkour works fine as usual – it’s not particularly complex and I definitely don’t want to keep doing it for hours, but it’s fun for a few hours and offers some great animation work.

Unfortunately, [i]Syndicate[/i] also suffers from a weird technical problem where the game sometimes renders in higher resolution than set in the graphics options. This might lead to distracting black bars during cutscenes. Follow [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=806615157]this guide[/url] to fix it.

Concluding, [i]Syndicate[/i] is less of a “greatest hits mix” and just “more of what worked before”. It’s a good [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] game that maybe got treated a bit too harshly at launch – but it’s also nothing more than that. Fans of the franchise will enjoy it and even newcomers might consider taking a look as there are only few ties to the previous games. But in the end, it’s no surprise that Ubisoft went for a major reinvention of the franchise next, as the “classic” [i]Assassin’s Creed[/i] formula had really run its course by that point in time.

[h1]Assassin’s Creed Syndicate Review[/h1]

[hr]
[h1]Overview[/h1]
Syndicate is not the most beloved entry in the series, but it has real charm. London looks and feels great, traversal is fast once the rope launcher clicks, and the twin-protagonist structure adds personality. Combat and some loop design are pretty basic, and it can feel less “Assassin Creed-y” because of the gang focus, yet it is still a fun, different spin that I would recommend.

[hr]
[h1]What It Is[/h1]
Set in 1868 during the Industrial Revolution, you play as twins Jacob and Evie Frye. The goal is to loosen Templar grip on London, building your gang The Rooks, and reclaiming districts through assassinations, takeovers, and story arcs tied to historical figures.

[hr]
[h1]World[/h1]
Victorian London is the star. Districts feel distinct, streets are busy, landmarks are climbable, and the art team sells the period really well. You also get a moving train hideout that circles the map, plus a short optional World War I rift later on. Ubisoft’s world building really lands here.

[hr]
[h1]Movement and Tools[/h1]
Parkour up and down from Unity returns, then the rope launcher changes everything. You can zip straight up facades or cast a line between rooftops to cross wide streets, which keeps flow high in a city with big avenues. Horse-drawn carriages are drivable and useful for quick escapes.

[hr]
[h1]Combat and Stealth[/h1]
Fist-forward brawling with simple timing. Weapons include cane-sword, kukri, and brass knuckles. It works, but it is pretty bare bones and can get repetitive. Stealth fares better: throwing knives, smoke, hallucinogenic darts, multi-target assassinations, and clear enemy vision cones make sneaking the more interesting path.

[hr]
[h1]Mission Design and Structure[/h1]
Black Box style assassinations give you multiple ways in, while district activities fill the map: gang strongholds, bounty hunts, child-labor liberations, Templar hunts, and collectibles. Taking territory to shift control to The Rooks is the loop, and it fits the setting even if it pushes the Creed angle into the background.

[hr]
[h1]Characters[/h1]
Jacob is cheeky chaos, Evie is precise and methodical. You can swap between them in free roam, and certain missions are character-locked. They are likable and carry scenes well, even if they do not evolve much across the story. Supporting cast is solid, and the “historical guest star” moments are fun.

[hr]
[h1]What Works[/h1]
[list]
[*] Lively, good-looking London with strong landmark density
[*] Rope launcher makes urban traversal fast and satisfying
[*] Stealth toolkit is the better half of the design
[*] Twin leads with different vibes keep the tone light
[*] Train hideout and territory system add identity
[/list]

[hr]
[h1]What Falls Short[/h1]
[list]
[*] Brawling is basic and gets samey in longer sessions
[*] Gang takeover loop can feel like checklist clearing
[*] Story ties to the Creed feel thin compared to older entries
[/list]

[hr]
[h1]Verdict[/h1]
Thumbs up. Not a classic, but a genuinely fun, stylish London adventure. If you want a beautiful city to free-run through, snappy stealth, and a different flavor for the series, Syndicate delivers. If you want deep combat or a heavy Creed focus, temper expectations.

Having devoted over 75 hours to the game, acquiring all the DLCs, and even buying the artbook, I can confidently say that I've embraced Assassin's Creed Syndicate as a true fan. This game became my cherished realm - a comforting place I could revisit time and again.

For me, Assassin's Creed Syndicate is a dream fulfilled, allowing us to step into the shoes of the intelligent Evie Frye, a refreshing and formidable female lead in the Assassin's Creed universe, and her charismatic sibling, Jacob Frye, who happens to be the funniest assassin ever. This adventure unfolds amidst the historically rich tapestry of 19th-century London - a city I've always yearned to explore.

Playing through the narrative, I found myself deeply invested in the Frye siblings' journey, their struggles, and their aspirations. Evie's dedication to preserving the Assassin's Creed with precision and intellect beautifully contrasts with Jacob's more impulsive and flamboyant approach. The world is meticulously designed, with landmarks like Big Ben and the River Thames brought to life with astounding accuracy. The downloadable content enhanced the gameplay experience by providing additional storylines and challenges, allowing me to extend my adventure in this fascinating world.

Oh, my. I never thought I'd enjoy an Assassin's Creed game this much ever again after playing the utter disaster that was Assassin's Creed Unity. I'm having so much fun with this game I literally just paused it right now and Alt+Tabbed into Steam to write this review.

To sum everything up really quickly: Combine the amazing ambiance and atmosphere of Assassin's Creed II with the sheer fun and satisfation of Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood and Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag and you get this game. It's that good. If you're a fan of the series, buy it right now and don't look back. Trust me.

For a bit more detail, read on.

Some background on me: I'm a monumental, long-time fan of this series. A history major in college, I reserved the first game on Xbox 360 and played it the day it came out in 2007, eager to see what a video game rendering of the Crusades would be like. [url=http://steamcommunity.com/id/greatjon_umber/recommended/33230/]Assassin's Creed II came along and struck me like Cupid's Arrow[/url]; the unrepentant love I have for that game still exists to this day and even motivated me to visit Florence and Venice multiple times in the past few years. I played AC3, didn't like it much, played Black Flag, loved it. 

Then Assassin's Creed Unity happened, and pretty much drove a rusty dagger through the heart of my love for this series. What an absolute disaster. [url=http://steamcommunity.com/id/greatjon_umber/recommended/289650/]I hated every bit of it[/url]. It caused me to all but abandon the series... Until now, almost a year after Syndicate's release, when I decided to give it a try despite my hatred for Ubisoft and all of the bad will I still hold from being burned by Unity, which still doesn't run on my PC.

And boy, am I glad I tried Syndicate. I have almost no complaints about this game. In fact, it's the best Assassin's Creed game I've played since Brotherhood, and maybe even better than that. It stands up there with Assassin's Creed II as the best game of the series. Yes, better than Black Flag. It's that good.

The game is drop dead gorgeous. Ambient occlusion and bloom make the lighting utterly beautiful, and the rain and water effects are jaw-dropping. The character textures are good but not great, but the environment textures are wonderful. Graphical prowess is nothing new for this game, though. What is strikingly better than recent efforts is the sheer immersion of Victorian London. I haven't felt so immersed in an Assassin's Creed setting since Florence and Venice in Assassin's Creed II. The NPC interactions on the street, ambient noise, and weather effects are all amazing. Drunks will sing, people will get into fights, there will be random shakedowns in alleys.There are evocative bills posted everywhere outside and indoor areas have Holmesian decorations like old couches and oil lamps. It's just fantastic the way that good film sets are fantastic; it adds so much atmosphere without you ever really noticing where it comes from unless you stop and serious examine your surroundings. There's so much to talk about that I can't possibly touch it all, but it all combines to a sum greater than its parts and transports you straight into the era in a way that few others games have. Maybe just Dishonored -- And that game was a fantasy only inspired by Victorian London.

Black Flag was a great game, but to me it didn't really feel like an Assassin's Creed game. It was more of a pirate game inspired by Assassin's Creed. Edward doesn't even become an assassin until the very end! Yet people still loved it, myself included. Arno was admittedly dull in Unity (a somewhat lesser rehash of Ezio Auditore but without the motivating factor of vengeance and half the charm), so to solve the problem of where to go with this protagonist, the developers give us two playable characters: Evie, the quintessential no-nonsense assassin who is completely dedicated to the creed (a la Altair in the first game), and Jacob, the loose cannon, troublemaking, bar brawling Englishman who isn't a serious assassin, only joining because his parents raised him to be one (a la Edward Kenway from Black Flag). And the system works perfectly. The two characters, between whom you can switch at any time, are the most well fleshed out playable characters to appear in this game in a long time. They each have chemistry, their dialogue is written well, and their voice actors are excellent. Motion capture serves well as they each have unique mannerisms. The skill trees can be individualized between them both, creating a drive to continue on playing and customizing to your liking. And gang upgrades and skill trees ensure that you'll spend hours just gathering money and items, staying up until 2:00 AM because "I just want to unlock one more thing", something I haven't felt about these games since the Apprentice missions in Brotherhood.

The gameplay itself provides ample opportunity to play it as either a brawler, a pure stealth venture, or something in between. Whatever you want, it's here, and they blend seamlessly into one another. Past Creed games have overloaded the player with too many tools, effectively eliminating any challenge the game poses. This game fixes that by giving you just enough to keep it interesting, but not so much that you're easily able to breeze through everything once you have all of the unlocks. The stealth sequences give you just enough tools to remain challenging, and the combat is less Assassin's Creed, more Batman Arkham, which is a good thing in that it provides depth to the experience. And traversal is easier and more satisfying than ever thanks to the hookshot. This game is so. Much. Fun.

The soundtrack is also noticeably better than recent entries into the series thanks to Austin Wintory's superb score of both subtle ambient tracks and crashing woodwinds and strings for the battle scenes. Again, the best score in an Assassin's Creed game since Jesper Kyd's watermark score in Assassin's Creed II.

If I do have one complaint about this game, it's the control. The improved traversal from Unity is here, but for some reason the Frye twins seem to respond to change of direction a bit more slowly, and deciding when to free run up is sometimes clunky. Everything feels more muddy than in previous titles, which can adversely affect some stealth sequences.

In order to assuage any worried about Ubisoft's bad PC ports in the past, I will say that this game runs superbly on my rig. This is the best running Assassin's Creed game I've played since Brotherhood. Even Black Flag was a bit more shaky. Unity ran around 50 FPS on high settings on my machine, this game is locked at 60 FPS with all settings maxed and I've seen very few bugs outside of normal fare for open world games.

Another plus is that, while they're still there (unfortunately), Ubisoft has greatly toned down the in-game microtransactions from Unity. Instead of popping up all over the map like in Unity, now they are relegated to being only an option in the menu, easily ignored. As a completionist I still get pissed off thinking about how annoying those microtransaction icons were in Unity. Despicable.

To sum it up: This is a fucking great game. It absolutely breaks my heart that this title was completely overlooked and did poorly financially upon release all due to Ubisoft's screwing the pooch and releasing Unity as a broken mess when it honestly could have been a good game with another year of development.

If you're a fan of the series and you're in the mood for some face and neck stabbing then you have to purchase this immediately. Don't wait like I did. It's worth an immediate buy. If you aren't a huge fan of the Assassin's Creed series and you just like open world action games like the Batman Arkham series, give Syndicate a whirl. I bet you'll like it.

Ah Syndicate, the game that had the misfortune of coming out during a time where people started to realize that Assassin's Creed games have overstayed their welcome especially after the departure of the modern day aspect starting from Unity. 

I had played it a little back when it first came out and it really didn't catch my attention due to it's horrible optimization (ran like crap on my 750Ti and 970 both). Deciding to clear my backlog, I revisited this game halfheartedly and gave it another chance. 

Clearly a LOT of work has been put into this game despite having several flaws regarding gameplay and story (which is barely there).

Starting with the cons :

- The main villain is the most useless antagonist I've ever seen in a video game, Joseph Starrick spends 95% of the time sitting in his chair and giving orders to his lieutenants, doing nothing himself. 
- No modern day at all, which is fundamentally the backbone of AC Games.
- Jacob and Evie barely have any missions together and I think they made a mistake by keeping their missions separate.
- The world is full of repetitive side tasks and is just there to increase the playtime (really not worth it, even if you're a completionist.)
- Animations feel wonkier when compared to Unity and it feels as thought there's a slight input lag (no, v sync was off the entire time and no other game has had this issue, also I used KB+M)
- The level up system gets quite annoying especially if you really want to craft a cool looking gauntlet or weapon, the game literally forces you to run around and open chest boxes or just buy the materials using MICROTRANSACTIONS, WHAT THE HECK UBI?

And now for the pros :

- A SEPARATE WW1 Mini Campaign with it's own playable character (unlocks after sequence 6).
- London is freaking AMAZING and the grappling hook is by far the best feature of this game since it's made to traverse easily due to the map's sheer verticality.
- You'll be impressed by the amount of detail put into the NPC's and the environment, you can come across small details like chimney sweepers, newspaper sellers, a goddamn street orchestra, and firemen extinguishing fire in a burning building.
- The train hide-out is a godsend.
- Jacob and Evie are great characters and have a lot of personality to them, especially when compared to Alexios/Kassandra and Arno even though they're not as memorable as Desmond, Ezio, Altair and Connor.
- The combat is pretty satisfying and has a lot of variety when it comes to combos and executions, not to mention the huge arsenal of tools that you get.
- Having the ability to recruit your gang members and sit back while they do your work is quite satisfying.
- You can also upgrade your gang as well as have a stable source of income which is quite helpful.
- Jack the Ripper is one of the best DLCs in the entire franchise, don't @me.
- Imo, the graphics are even better than Origins and Odyssey's, and the game almost looks photorealistic, ESPECIALLY during the night time.
- The optimization has somewhat improved and the game is completely playable on a mixture of Very High and Ultra settings.

Verdict : 

It's a solid 7/10 and a decent game that just came out at a time where people were simply tired of Assassin's Creed.
I suggest that you pick this up during a sale and play it in short bursts to prevent yourself from burning out.

For an "Assassin's Creed", not at all a bad game but also not one of the Best Ones either. The Story is boring but gameplay is fine.
But as an open world game, it's really good.. Play it and enjoy it.

This game is also the last Assassin's Creed before they changed the gameplay, so the game is as simple as those Assassin's Creed use to be.

The environment is this game looks clean. Victorian London and it's streets are big. The Architecture in this game in beautiful, spot on from historical standpoint, the world design itself is very good. Streets are filled with people & so many buildings have fully explorable interiors that makes this open world a must see. The scaling of everything in the massive.

The basic missions you embark on are pretty normal as far as "Assassin's Creed" games go with the usual objectives of tailing, killing and kidnapping. Parkour is as good as any assassin's creed game, driving carriages and rampaging on the streets of London with it is a lot of fun, hell, you can even drift with horse drawn carriages. Fighting enemies on train tops & carriage tops and kicking them off the running train & carriages gives a feeling of much satisfying finishing blow. Combat, Stealth and Ecosystem is also very good. Combat system a little different from other AC.

But many things in this game has upsides and downsides.
For example.. The scaling of everything in the massive, the roads. the buildings, the trains etc.. the sense of scale really adds a feeling to the game.. jumping from rooftops to assassinate your target etc feels great.. but then again, the buildings are so far apart that it creates issue with the free-running when you have to move from rooftops of one side of the road to the other side of the road or if you're chasing someone or avoiding someone who's chasing you, it takes so much time to often climb the building or get down from building bcoz the roads are way too wide which makes those buildings far from each other creating issue of not being able to jump directly to the rooftops of other side of the road.. that problem only gets solved when you get the grappling hook to easily glide from one side to the other side of the road. So everything has both it's upsides and downsides.

Overall a good open world game.

Full disclosure: I only got into AC with Odyssey because the vast open world arpg was my jam (still is). I had no beef with more stuff like that being made and did not care at all that it was under the AC name. Odyssey is still my personal favorite comfort game. But after spending even a small amount of time in Syndicate, I think I finally [i] get [/i] what "the fans" of the originals felt like they were suddenly deprived of when the style changed. It's clear this is a stealth game first and foremost and, to my delight, it also happens to be a huge open world arpg. But it's the fact that the game is as fleshed-out as any other aaa game but focused on that assassin lifestyle is what makes it special. Well, actually the world of this game is also so dang special. It's really a beautiful city. I've never seen anything quite like the Thames, with all its boats blasting through it, in any other game. They nailed the scale of the city and made it seem overflowing with life. The music jumps OFF when things get intense and it's excellent. What a delight. And on top of it all the structure and flow of the whole game is right in line with my favorite game: the Ubisoft open world. Engaging, immersive, mechanically sound - can't ask for more. It's a very classy production all-around. I really slept on this one.

Assassins Creed syndicate would be a very good Assassins Creed game if there werent so many bugs. 


Good things:
- Story
- World
- Side quests (some of them)
- Mechanics
- Graphics
- Soundtrack
- 2 characters mechanics
- Combat 
- A lot of historical apparences



Bad things:
- A LOT of bugs
- Repetetive side quests (some of them)
- Not being able to fast travel while doing missions
- Gang mechanics are rarely useful



Story: 
The story is about two grown english twins, that are already in the Assassin order.
Their main objective is simple.
Take over the victorian london by killing the cruel templars and their companions that are ruling london. 
While being busy with that, they also need to secure the “traditional in the series” piece/s of eden. 
Now for the quality of the story.
Assassins creed is known to have two story lines in each game. 
One modern and one “acient”. 
If i would have to sum it up, the modern story line is pretty mid.
However, talking about the “acient” story line, its not that bad as some people say.
I will even say, that i actually enjoyed i. 
By the way, if you like historical apparences in the Assassins creed series, i think you will like this story line more. 


World:
What can i say for this topic other than i really liked the world.
If i would have to “remove” my opinion on victorian london, the graphics, the coloring, the npcs and the world structuring overall was just amazing.
Especially for a game that is nearly 10 years old. 


Side quests (some of them):
The reason why i wrote “some of them” for this topic is simple.
There are two versions of side quests in this game.
Story focused side quests and district liberation side quests.
Starting with the “bad” ones, the district liberation side quests are very repetetive.
For the comparison, its kinda similar to the first Assassins Creed game, even tho in the first Assassins Creed, it wasnt just side quests, but kinda the whole game. 
To be exact, the side quests arent bad, but every district that you can “liberate” has them  and they are basically the same but with more difficult enemyes. 
I know, they are just side quests and there isnt really a reason to play all of them, but if you are trying to complete the full game, it gets kinda grindy and after one or two districts, it isnt just fun. 
For the more story focused side quests i must say, that i enjoyed them.
The reasons behind why i enjoyed them are simple.
They were:
- Original (atleast some of them).
- Focused a lot on historical characters.
- Interesting.
- Fun.
- Short/long enough.


Mechanics:
The mechanics in this game are decent.
I enjoyed using the new zipline, that helps climbing more buldings faster and overall improves the parkour experience.
Another mechanic which i enjoyed was the driving.
To be specific:
- The “combat”.
- The physics
- The boost option
Another mechanic which i enjoyed was the 
“2 characters mechanic”.
Its mainly because of the different playstyles that each character has, but also because of some unique perks in the skill tree, even tho there really isnt many of them.
This game also focuses a lot on gang mechanics, as you can see in the trailers etc.
Dont get me wrong, calling your gang members to help you etc is fun and it really gives you the feeling of a “gang leader”, however it isnt really usefull, which is kinda shame. 
The last mechanic i want to talk about is the 
“Not being able to fast travel while doing missions”. 
I understand that it could potentionally make some missions easier than it should have been, however most of the time, its just  annoying. 


Combat: 
Personally, i really enjoyed the combat.
It isnt necessarily easy, but also not necessarily hard. 
Its build more on doing comboes with some quicktime events, which i really liked.
Other than that, it is also fast and brutal, as it should have been based on the setting. 


Soundtrack: 
All i can say for the soundtrack, is that its good.
Maybe iam just dumb, but i think soundtracks in games have one job.
That job is about fitting in the setting or a specific moment. 
By the way, a small reminder: i definitely dont think that its one of the best, i just think its good. 


A LOT of bugs:
This is my main issue with this game and also why am i giving this game lower rating than it should have based on the takes above.
I know, this is my 32nd review, so i havent played a lot of games i guess, but still.
To the moment i launched and played this game, i havent experienced this many bugs in any other game.
For example:
- Physics glitches - mainly with  carriages.
- Mission glitches - game missunderstanding my death with the death of my assassination target (wtf).
- Npcs dying just because they exit the carrige the wrong way (wtf v2).
- My character literally flying because the carrige did something (yes iam still clueless about some bugs that happened). 
- And so on.
Either way, its stil playable, however it definitely messes up the experience. 


Overall:
Overall, its a great game and for sure underrated Assassins Creed game.
(If i forget about the bugs of course).
On sale for 10 euros, its worth it, if you like Assassins creed games or you are just interested in the setting.

In my honest opinion, Syndicate was a really enjoyable experience from a guy who played nearly all of the AC games. I will try to be short and tell you what it shines at and what it is bad at.

Story:
       The story in this part of the AC history is quite intresting and enjoyable to see play through. The 2 main characters, Jacob and Evie Frye are prob on my top list of fav AC guys, but top spot will always be Edward Kenaway from AC4:BF. These twins are enjoyable to play as, their personalities are complex, with own motivations and well developed minds. Jacob is for me so hardly to not be my fav character from these games, he is the funniest one out of all AC guys from before, has charisma, his reasons are strong and you just enjoy seeing him talk. Evie also is the 2nd playable woman character in this series. I was skeptical at first about her, but she is one of my fav female personas in fictional art. As her brother Jacob, she is very funny, charisma, enjoyable to see her play around. Overall i love both of them and their interactions with each other are just the best thing in this game.
        The story is set around industrial England period, mostly industrial London in 1868. This time, compared to the other games we are in more advanced period of time. The story is intresting, with more good characters besides the 2 twins, most of them being good, but the main antagonist of this game is just really bad. Crawford Starrick is prob one of the most underdeveloped guys i've ever seen so far. His motivations are kinda dull, just like the other Templar antagonists from previous games, but at least the others were better in the character development. In this game, you only see this guy in cinematics, mostly at the end of each sequence up to sequence 9 where you have to kill him in the last mission. Even there the boss fight with him is utter bad, i really don't know who came up with this design for this guy, was rather dissapointed with him overall, but not such a let down to hate the story. Story is all in all enjoyable, you will not get bored.


Gameplay:
If you played AC Unity before this you will immediately see that this game is very similar to the previous one. Indeed, it's kinda the same game when it comes to gameplay, but with slightly different mechanics. The combat is mostly the same, but in AC Syndicate i felt like it was a little bit easier to fight than in Unity. It kinda reminded me of the older titles like AC4, Rogue or AC3 where you could fight armies alone just by pressing counter and LMB. No it isn't the exact case, but press counter and LMB mostly works if you know how to time your attacks and counters. The gear system is back here too, you have to find schematics for better gear or just get it by completing main missions/side ones. The game is huge, prob as huge as Unity or even bigger, but the biggest dissapointment for me was that the collectables here won't appear on the map unless you are near them or find them with eagle vision. Really bad, Unity did this too most of the time and that for a guy like me who wants the 100% sync is really bad and time consuming. The only 2 things that make this game different in gameplay from the other ones are the rope you can launch from your assassin gauntlent, very useful for navigating around the city more faster and easier and the other thing is that here we have carrieges which are pulled by horses. Gives you a 19th century GTA vibe.

Audio:
The game sounds very good in all aspects, the voice acting is on top, the characters giving you feelings and emotions. Evie and Jacob are perfect here, no comment. 

Multiplayer:
NO! Thank god not this time.

Graphics:
This one is an obv downgrade from Unity. It doesn't mean it looks really bad or something, but when compared to Unity, the most obv kinda clone of this game or vice versa, it looks a little bit downgraded overall. London looks gorgeous, the amount of details put in it are amazing and the game can run pretty well on older hardware too. I tested this on a 750ti and it ran pretty smoothly at 1080p, tho with medium settings. Yes the game had the ocasional freezes, but on the newer and more capable hardware there is no problem.

Would i recommend this to any AC fan or a new commer to the series? For one who played other AC games this will be what the others gave him so far and more. For a new commer? Yes. It's a very good game and i can't really say you will get bored easily, only if you really don't like it at all. But i would not buy at full price. I didn't get it at full neither, got it when it was like 10 euros with Jack the Ripper DLC too at reduced cost.

Assassin’s Creed Syndicate is an action adventure game developed and published by Ubisoft, releasing in October 2015 for the PS4, Xbox One and PC. This is the 9th game in the Assassin’s Creed series so far. The game is run using the AnvilNext 2.0 engine, which was used in AC Unity and Rainbow Six Siege. 

For the game play, most will probably be already well aware of what to expect from an Assassin’s Creed game. You play as one of two playable characters, Evie and Jacob Frye.  A new, welcome mechanic to the game is a rope launcher, allowing the characters to quickly scale larger buildings and to create their own zip-lines for easier travel between buildings too. The combat system is at its best again with a very easy to use control set.  The game is set in London, and you are able to freely roam the city completing all kinds of quests, finding collectables and locating treasure scattered around the world. Whilst the game play is considered the same as the rest of the games, I still really enjoyed it.

Graphically, Syndicate looks gorgeous, I sadly was not able to run the game at 4k, but was able to push all of the graphics up to max on 1440. The City of London just looks amazing. The textures are of all high quality, animation is almost seemly showing on all of the characters. It is a huge improvement over the previous entries to the series. Voice acting is spot on with the classic London accent on all characters found throughout the game. 

You should not expect a challenging game when playing Syndicate, as long as you stick to the areas of London that is within your level range, you probably won’t die at all. You can challenge yourself by going to the higher level zones before you should, but I found myself to getting completely overrun by more powerful enemies quicker than normal. The game’s skills trees are very well designed to let you build your two characters to specialise in different trees. I went for Evie being the more stealth oriented character and Jacob the more hand-fisted of the two. I really liked having the option of the two characters as it lets you choose the right head for the job you have been tasked to do. 

Like I said above, the city is jam-packed full of things to do, gang wars, freeing laboured children, finding rare wine or searching for treasure. There are hours of content to be found after you complete the game, with plenty of side quests to take on as well. This was one of the few Assassins’ Creed games that I actually really enjoyed doing the optional tasks in.  

I have been playing Syndicate for about 50 hours so far. The main story only takes about half of that. I wouldn’t say there is a huge level of replay ability in this game, as the story is linear and the lack of any difficulty options means you can’t replay the game in a sort of New Game + mode. Although I am very happy with the amount of hours I have put into the game so far and not many people about the amount of content on offer in this game. 

Thankfully I didn’t have any technical problems. I wasn’t able to run at 4k, because it is simply too taxing at this moment in time. But the game ran as smooth as butter at 1440p in 60 fps. The game is very well optimized and loading times are almost none-existent. I played with a controller and I would suggest you do to as the combat system just matches up well with it. 

To sum up, Assassin’s Creed Syndicate is one of the better games in the series, coming close to Black Flag as the best.  The characters are probably the most loveable of all of the series so far, with Evie being the first female protagonist. The game has plenty of content, and shows off extremely high production values in the graphics and sound departments. The lack of any technical problems also counts as a major positive for the AC series too given past releases not being so smooth. As with all recently released games in this series, you should expect a premium price tag, and this is no different at £39, 99. If you can wait it out another few months you can probably get it for £30, but I would say the game is even worth it at full price right now.

Now for the Pros: Victorian London looks great, it's gorgeous and well detailed overall. The rope launcher was a nice addition too. The game was decent enough customization (although less than unity) and most of the outfits look great on the characters. I did not experience any major bugs either. Recruiting gang members to infiltrate regions was also quite enjoyable. There are many tools in the game and the stealth aspect is quite strong.

Now for the Cons: The story is quite boring tbh, i never felt the need to know what would happen next. The protagonist Evie and Jacob Frye are just quite bad, Victorian London is a dark setting with child labour and poverty and people getting opressed but the Frye twins present this upbeat tone and act like clowns and the problem is.. their jokes don't really land. Its a weird choice overall. Also Evie and Jacob are pretty much the same, the only difference is at the end of the skill tree which you won't really unlock until the game is almost done which takes away from the point of having two different protagonist in the first place. The villain is a generic bad guy who wants to take over London and also wants the Shroud of Eden. The game looks graphically worse than Unity, the draw distance is super low due to an omnipresent fog, which also reduces performance, because if you remove the fog, you will get a performance boost and realize how bad the city looks at the far end. The combat is the worst I've ever seen, it's literally just button mashing and looks super cartoonish. The weapon types are pretty much none, there are some daggers, cane swords and knuckles. There's also a lack of proper animations and the whole game can start to feel a little repetitive. There are also 40 different side quests, which actually mean that there are 4, copy and pasted 10 times in different regions (cough *dunkey reviews* cough). The parkour is a huge step back from unity, in Unity where you could freely jump about and create cool paths, well now even with similar animation, Jacob lacks the agility, the game also just won't let you freely jump and will constantly try to hold our hands thus reducing player agency. The city although designed very well isn't one for parkour, the streets are super wide and you'd have to use the rope launcher which again being a cool gadget, just throws the parkour out of the windows and becomes a Batman game. The rope launcher also is just terribly under used, it would have been super cool to use it in combat and the kills could've been brutal, maybe even in stealth, even earlier games like Rogue have used rope darts to do similar stuff, why couldn't Syndicate do it too. The horse carriage are also just super weird to handle. The game also has super weird cutscenes in a few moments, and this is greatly magnified in the Last Maharaja DLC. Even GTA San Andreas, a game from 2004 had better cutscenes. The Season Pass of the game doesn't include all the DLCs. The game also has microtransactions.

Now for the DLCs: 
Do not buy the Last Maharaja DLC, its just terrible with the dumbest AI and some of the most terrible mission designs in the game. I'm an Indian and I still had no interest with this DLC. 
Jack The Ripper DLC however was quite enjoyable, its presents a more serious tone, there's a slight sense on mystery about Jack's Identity, the Fear Takedowns are really good, being able to play as Jack the Ripper was slightly unsettling cuz I don't really want to control a serial killer but it presented some good moments of the narrative. Jacob and Evie are also a lot older and wiser and not clowns anymore which was great. The Sherlock Holmes Series styled investigation sequences were also well made.
The Dreadful Crimes is the 3rd and final DLC for the game and *IS NOT* included in the season pass. This DLC goes further into the Sherlock type Investigations and tbh they are really interesting, its quite nice overall but the fact that it isn't in the season pass is still quite bad
The cosmetic items such as the outfits and stuff look nice, it depends on person to person if you like them, although almost all the outfits in the game look great

If you liked the classic Assassin's Creed formula, this was the last gasp of that era. 

London is well crafted, gritty, and exciting to explore - in typical AC fashion. The writing is just okay which is about all you can expect as the writers contort themselves through their ever more convoluted universe to make another franchise entry. The Abstergo story line is effectively abandoned in favor of focusing on the historical Assassin's - but even these two aren't particularly compelling. 

Game play wise, the game divides itself in two with one protagonist focused on stealth, the other focused on combat. Perhaps inspired by the success of GTA V's multiple protagonists, AC Syndicate gives them very distinctly different missions. While fun, the combination of missions and narratives still fails to live up to the Ezio trilogy. 

Functionally, the game is better than older AC games. You should not run into issues with frames being too high or other similar issues. Controllers are natively supported as well.

A significant improvement over AC: Unity but not without its flaws. Syndicate stars twins Jacob and Evie Frye set in Victorian London. As always with AC games, the world is beautiful and feels alive. The Frye twins are interesting protagonists and the game play aspect of being able to switch between characters for a slightly different play style is a nice change.

Unfortunately Syndicate also shares some similar problems as previous AC installments, namely repetition. The world map is filled with side missions and collectibles, alas most of them are pretty much the same and once you've collected a few vintage beer bottles or pressed flowers there's not much fun in finding more, unless you want to try different color schemes for your outfits in the crafting menu.

Speaking of crafting, the crafting system has been expanded this time around and you'll be able to craft new and more powerful weapons and armor which is a nice addition to the game. Skills and perks have been improved as well but at only 10 levels max it won't take you that long to reach the highest level.

Some side missions will have you encounter famous people from the Victorian era but game play wise these missions don't do anything new. The main missions do provide alternate ways of completing objectives, which is nice but in the end I found that it just didn't provide enough entertainment to revisit.

As with most AC games, don't expect great optimization or a steady frame rate and be prepared to struggle with numerous bugs and graphical glitches, though it's certainly not as bad as AC: Unity.

If you're a fan of the AC series then Syndicate is worth picking up. If not then this game will not change your mind as it's really more of them same except in a different setting.

I'm struggling to think of more nice things to say, so now here's why I think Syndicate is a steaming pile of bloody shite:

[h1] Gameplay & Mechanics [/h1]

-This series has downgraded since Unity. The increased difficulty is gone, as well as the weapon diversity and skill building. I understand we're in 1868 London, it probably wouldn't be acceptable to waltz around the streets with a claymore but surely they could program more than three melee weapons and one type of handgun into Syndicate?
-The side missions are repetitive beyond belief and no fun at all. They've locked the higher tier gear and important items behind them, so get grinding if you want em. This is a choice they've made to push the Helix Credit system, which is an offer to spend real money in order to purchase "shortcuts". Because who has time to play an actual fun game anymore, right? This system was present in Unity as well, but Ubisoft has since learned how not to make side quests enjoyable.
-There's only 10 levels to achieve and you'll be maxed out before you even do a quarter of the side missions, so in a way the above point is entirely moot since you'll be blowing through the entire game's enemies with low level gear anyways. Syndicate relies on your measure of self restraint not to accidentally overlevel yourself instead of pacing the game.

[h1] Plot & Characters [/h1]

-The story both doesn't exist and is contrived as hell. Our protagonists head to London with the chief goal of killing Templars, finding the magic relic bullshite and "freeing" the city. It never goes deeper than that, ever. The first 15 minutes would have you believe otherwise, as Jacob and Evie's handler says they aren't supposed to go to London because they need to heed the word of the council for reasons. Luckily for them the outside world and its consequences stop existing as soon as they get to London.
-The protagonists and all the characters have the personality and motivations of a wet noodle. Jacob and Evie do little more than pop one liners while they kill people. Their only character dynamic is Daddy Issues; I wish I was joking. Their allies have such little presence it's almost as if the Assassins took over London without any outside help at all, each one appearing with a few lines of paltry dialogue and a handful of cutscenes to establish them. I couldn't possibly blame someone for not remembering any names outside the famous people. With no context these minor characters somehow already know all the important details about this secret society war waged for centuries.
-The main antagonist is a moustache-twirling card-carrying Saturday morning cartoon villain, and go figure he looks like one too. They spend far too long showcasing his evil curly moustache and dark, sunken eyes as he monologues about child labour and controlling the minds of the citizenry all for this vague bullshite future he's got planned for London. I was sick of hearing his name the 3rd time I heard it. One hilarious moment that sticks out is a cutscene of him playing the piano and singing softly in memoriam of his dear cousin you just murdered. This is a humanizing moment for our villain as he's shown to care about something more than just power--why is the camera panning over his revolver, it's not like he's going to use it hereOH there it is. Shot his manservant for daring to interrupt his sad moment. He's EEEEEVUUL guys, don't forget that.
-I've seen people praise Syndicate for bringing back the memory corridors, the one on one dialogue between the assassin and their target they just killed. In previous titles they used these moments to draw in-depth comparisons to the sheer difference in methods and mindset between the two contradicting ideologies trying to answer the same question: What's best for humanity? If you watch AC1 and AC3's memory corridors vs Syndicate's you realize rather quickly they wasted the potential for that here. Jacob and Evie downright insult those they kill, either side throwing their cheap accusations and vague motivations around like children arguing over their toys. It hurts to watch but thankfully each one barely lasts a minute.

[h1] HOLY SHIT BUGS [/h1]

I'm sure this is unique to every player but I seriously thought they patched these bugs out years ago.
-I lost count of my CTDs after the 8th time. Somehow Unity ran better, and that's REALLY saying something.
-Stuttering and freezing is commonplace. Riding horse carriages causes a 1-2 second stutter while the game tries to load your surroundings in. Outside of carriages it isn't uncommon to just freeze in place for a good 5, 10 seconds. Changing graphic settings did nothing to alleviate these issues.
-The parkour is still slightly imprecise. Sometimes you'll fly off somewhere different from where you wanted to go or just doggy paddle in midair. A little annoying, but luckily not common.
-I don't know if it's the close proximity some missions and side activities have with each other, but a few times absolute chaos would just break out completely out of my control and ruin mission objectives.
-Syndicate cannot handle overlays or background processes in the slightest. It's optimized so poorly everything slows down and creates more opportunities for crashing. I've never had a game die on me simply because a friend messaged me on Steam.

[h1] Stupid Nitpicks [/h1]

-The little disclaimer at the start of the game that says the creators were a multicultural team of various religious beliefs is gone, replaced by one that says Syndicate was made by a team of people with multiple sexual orientations and genders. I guess that matters more now, since AC is no longer a series about different groups all fighting over how people ought to live. I wouldn't even bother bringing it up if it wasn't an obvious ploy to satisfy those gremlins pretending to be progressive journalists & corporate heads that make up the video game industry today. I just wouldn't be able to sleep at night if I didn't know gays and transsexuals couldn't make games in the current year!

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
